boards.school_name: University of North Carolina School of the Arts
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UNCSA campus spaces with documented student uses, from meeting and study areas to creative-community venues.

cards.title: Hanes Student Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus center for meals, meetings, and activities
cards.notes: Use the Commons as a practical meeting point: it is documented for eating, socializing, meetings, and organizing activities.
cards.short_summary: A central student-services and gathering building.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says Hanes Student Commons provides space for students, faculty, and staff to eat, socialize, meet, and organize activities.
cards.access_notes: Campus facility; consult Student Affairs for meeting-space reservations.

cards.title: Eisenberg Social Hall
cards.subtitle: Ground floor of Hanes Student Commons
cards.notes: Plan student gatherings or attend campus programming here; the hall has ballroom and multipurpose-room configurations.
cards.short_summary: A flexible social hall inside the student commons.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA describes Eisenberg Social Hall as a large ballroom and smaller multipurpose room that can be used separately or combined.
cards.access_notes: Groups reserve Commons spaces through the Campus Portal Calendar or Student Affairs.

cards.title: The Well and TV Lounge
cards.subtitle: Inside Hanes Student Commons
cards.notes: Choose this named lounge when coordinating a low-key break or a casual conversation between classes and rehearsals.
cards.short_summary: A designated lounge within the campus hub.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA lists The Well and TV lounge among the facilities in Hanes Student Commons.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hanes Student Commons; access is subject to campus building operations.

cards.title: Hanes Student Commons Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Computer lab in Hanes Student Commons
cards.notes: Use the named computer lab for a focused work session when a shared campus workstation is more useful than a lounge seat.
cards.short_summary: A workstation option in the student commons.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA lists a Computer Lab among the facilities in Hanes Student Commons.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hanes Student Commons; use follows current campus technology and building policies.

cards.title: Library and Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus library and study destination
cards.notes: Meet for a quiet study block or join the documented Wednesday Mindful Lunch Hour held in the Library.
cards.short_summary: The campus library also hosts a weekly mindfulness gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA identifies the Library and Learning Commons on its campus map and says its Mindful Lunch Hour meets in the Library every Wednesday.
cards.access_notes: The campus map identifies this as Library and Learning Commons; verify current library access before visiting.

cards.title: Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Next to Artist Village
cards.notes: Schedule a movement break, group exercise, or student-organized game-club activity using the gym, aerobic room, and weight area.
cards.short_summary: Student-accessible fitness space with classes and game-club use.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says students are automatically Fitness Center members; the center offers group exercise and student-organized sport and game clubs.
cards.access_notes: UNCSA lists semester hours: Monday–Thursday 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; Friday 7 a.m.–6 p.m.; weekends 11 a.m.–5 or 10 p.m. Check seasonal changes.

cards.title: Artist Village

cards.short_summary: A residence hall built with several shared student spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says Artist Village includes gaming areas, community lounges, kitchens, studies on each floor, and laundry facilities.
cards.access_notes: College residence hall; exterior doors use computerized keyless entry and are restricted to UNCSA affiliates.

cards.title: Connector Building
cards.subtitle: High School Life community and study building
cards.notes: High school students can use its study rooms, computer lab, arts studio, kitchen, and multipurpose social-gathering space.
cards.short_summary: A High School Life building combining study, creative, and gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says the Connector Building houses High School Life offices, study rooms, a computer lab, arts studio, kitchen, and a large multipurpose space for student social gatherings.

cards.title: Daniels Plaza

cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA's undergraduate orientation schedule places New Student Welcome Sessions at Daniels Plaza.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus location; event setup and availability vary by the university calendar.

cards.title: Crawford Hall
cards.subtitle: Gray Building performance venue

cards.short_summary: A music-complex venue used for student programs and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA's orientation schedule lists an Open Mic Night in Gray Building's Crawford Hall, and UNCSA identifies it as a campus venue.
cards.access_notes: Performance and event access depends on the program; consult the UNCSA calendar or venue staff.

cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Mill Creek Loop at Historic Bethabara and says the park’s trails are open free of charge.

cards.title: Visit Bethabara’s Historic Gardens
cards.subtitle: Historic Bethabara Park
cards.notes: Make the gardens a calm conversation stop, then continue through the grounds; respect planted areas and posted preservation guidance.
cards.short_summary: Named gardens within the free Historic Bethabara grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Historic Bethabara Park’s grounds and gardens are open free of charge all day, all year.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park, grounds, gardens, and trails are free; visitor-center hours vary seasonally.

cards.title: Browse Central Library
cards.subtitle: 660 W. Fifth Street, Winston-Salem
cards.notes: Choose a floor to browse together, use free library resources, or check the calendar for a public program before heading downtown.
cards.short_summary: Downtown public library with free access to resources, services, and programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Forsyth County Central Library states that it provides free access to a wide variety of resources, services, and programs.

cards.subtitle: University of North Carolina School of the Arts campus
cards.notes: Check UNCSA’s event listings and attend an event marked free; confirm audience eligibility and ticket details before inviting friends.
cards.short_summary: UNCSA documents that many campus events are free.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA states that there are many free events on campus, alongside separately ticketed performances.
cards.access_notes: Availability, audience eligibility, and any reservation requirements vary by event; verify the individual event listing.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina School of the Arts
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented UNCSA rituals and recurring arts-community practices, from a campus-wide holiday production to Pickle-led celebrations.

cards.title: The annual UNCSA Nutcracker
cards.subtitle: Holiday production since 1966
cards.notes: Plan around the December run and look for the cross-school collaboration: Dance, Music, and Design & Production students all contribute.
cards.short_summary: A recurring UNCSA production that has been performed annually by students since 1966.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA states that students have performed its production of “The Nutcracker” annually under faculty and staff direction since 1966.
cards.source_title: “The Nutcracker,” presented by Mercedes-Benz of Winston-Salem, live at the Stevens Center Dec. 9-18
cards.access_notes: Performance attendance is generally ticketed; check the current production page for dates and ticket details.

cards.title: Campus Night dress rehearsal
cards.subtitle: UNCSA’s final Nutcracker rehearsal
cards.notes: If invited as part of the campus community, use this final dress rehearsal to support the cast and crew before the public run begins.
cards.short_summary: Students, faculty and staff attend the final dress rehearsal to support the production team.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA describes the final Nutcracker dress rehearsal as “campus night,” when students, faculty and staff attend to support the cast and crew.
cards.source_title: Behind the Scenes at UNCSA's “The Nutcracker”
cards.access_notes: This is a campus-community rehearsal, not a guaranteed public event; confirm eligibility and access with UNCSA.

cards.title: Preparatory dancers in the Party Scene
cards.subtitle: Auditioned children’s roles
cards.notes: Watch for Preparatory Dance students in the Party Scene; the roles are auditioned and connect the school’s younger dancers to the production.
cards.short_summary: UNCSA’s Preparatory Dance students audition to perform the Party Scene children’s roles.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA reports that Preparatory Dance students perform as the children in the Nutcracker Party Scene and must audition for those roles.
cards.source_title: Behind the Scenes at UNCSA's “The Nutcracker”
cards.access_notes: This is part of a ticketed performance; participation is by audition.

cards.title: The student Nutcracker orchestra
cards.subtitle: Live score performed by School of Music students
cards.notes: Listen for the live student orchestra alongside the dancers; it is a concrete way the conservatory’s music and dance training meet on one production.
cards.short_summary: School of Music students perform the Nutcracker score as the production’s orchestra.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA states that School of Music students comprise the Nutcracker orchestra.
cards.source_title: Behind the Scenes at UNCSA's “The Nutcracker”
cards.access_notes: Hear the orchestra during a scheduled Nutcracker performance; ticket requirements vary by season.

cards.title: Sweeping and reusing stage snow
cards.subtitle: A backstage Nutcracker practice
cards.notes: Notice the snow effect, then explore UNCSA’s behind-the-scenes coverage to see how the translucent plastic snow is cleaned and reused between shows.
cards.short_summary: Each performance uses artificial snow that the production cleans and reuses.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says each Nutcracker performance uses 50 pounds of translucent-plastic snow, which is cleaned and reused.
cards.source_title: Behind the Scenes at UNCSA's “The Nutcracker”
cards.access_notes: Backstage work areas are not public; view the effect from a scheduled performance.

cards.source_title: Capturing memories: Relive the excitement of UNCSA Homecoming
cards.access_notes: Occurs during Homecoming; consult UNCSA’s current Homecoming announcements for dates and participation details.

cards.title: Find the student commons
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus gathering space
cards.notes: Walk to Hanes Student Commons and note its dining, mail, wellness and Student Affairs services so you know where to return during the week.
cards.short_summary: Identify the campus hub and its practical student services.
cards.evidence_claim: The official campus map lists Hanes Student Commons with Eisenberg Social Hall, Dining Hall, Pickle Jar, P.O.D. Market, Wellness Center, Mail Center and Student Affairs offices.
cards.access_notes: Campus services and building access can vary; check the relevant office before a special trip.

cards.title: Locate the Library and Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · study and research waypoint
cards.notes: Add the Library and Learning Commons to your mental map, then use the student-services page to reach the library’s current information and resources.
cards.short_summary: Make a future study-and-research stop easy to find.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA lists the Library and Learning Commons on its campus map and links students to Library services.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library directly for current access and service details.

cards.title: Pause at Daniels Plaza
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · central outdoor landmark
cards.notes: Use Daniels Plaza as a meet-up landmark for a campus walk, then continue toward the nearby performance and academic buildings shown on the official map.
cards.short_summary: Choose a named central landmark for an easy regroup point.
cards.evidence_claim: Daniels Plaza is identified as a named location on UNCSA’s official campus map.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is generally route-dependent; follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Spot the ACE Exhibition Complex
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · performance-venue orientation
cards.notes: Walk by the ACE Exhibition Complex and identify its Main, Gold and Babcock theatres on the map; check the performance calendar before planning an event visit.
cards.short_summary: Connect several named theatre spaces to one campus complex.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s campus map identifies the ACE Exhibition Complex and its Main Theatre, Gold Theatre and Babcock Theatre.
cards.access_notes: Performance access is event-specific; use the official calendar for availability and tickets.

cards.title: Recognize Performance Place
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · theatre cluster
cards.notes: Find Alex Ewing Performance Place and note the Freedman, Catawba and Patrons theatres listed there; save the calendar for future program details.
cards.short_summary: Learn one of UNCSA’s major on-campus performance locations.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA lists Alex Ewing Performance Place among its campus performance venues and identifies Freedman, Catawba and Patrons theatres there on the campus map.
cards.access_notes: Venue entry depends on the scheduled program and its admission terms.

cards.title: Find Watson Hall
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · music-complex landmark
cards.notes: Locate Watson Hall in the School of Music Complex and check the official performance listings when you want to attend a recital or concert.
cards.short_summary: Add a principal music venue to your campus route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA identifies Watson Chamber Music Hall in the School of Music Complex and describes it as the principal venue for School of Music faculty and guest-artist concert series.
cards.access_notes: Programs and entry are event-specific; consult the official performance calendar.

cards.title: Note Hood Recital Hall
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · intimate recital venue
cards.notes: Mark Hood Recital Hall in the Gray Building for a future student recital, and confirm the individual event’s details before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Recognize a small named venue used for recitals.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA identifies Hood Recital Hall in the Gray Building and describes it as the smallest on-campus performance venue, with 39 seats.
cards.access_notes: Entry and timing depend on the scheduled recital or event.

cards.title: Pass the de Mille Theatre
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · dance and opera venue
cards.notes: Locate the Agnes de Mille Theatre beside the Workplace complex, then watch the official calendar for a suitable dance concert or opera workshop program.
cards.short_summary: Learn a named campus theatre tied to dance and opera activity.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA states that the Agnes de Mille Theatre is used primarily for School of Dance concerts and A. J. Fletcher Opera Institute workshops and productions.
cards.access_notes: Attendance requires a scheduled program; review event-specific admission details.

cards.title: Choose a Sunday performance
cards.subtitle: Sunday planning · performances, recitals or screenings
cards.notes: Open the official performance calendar and choose an upcoming under-21-safe event that fits your schedule; confirm the venue, ticket status and start time on its listing.
cards.short_summary: Turn campus orientation into a specific arts plan.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s performance calendar lists upcoming events, and the university states that film screenings and student recitals are among events offered free of charge, while selected events have individual prices.
cards.access_notes: Check the individual listing for the current date, venue, admission and any ticket requirement.
